scored_idea.original_idea: Use activation patching and circuit ablation (TransformerLens) on a small model prompted to be deceptive vs. honest. Identify candidate circuits and test whether ablating them reduces deceptive output without degrading honest communication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires advanced mechanistic interpretability skills: activation patching, circuit ablation, TransformerLens proficiency. These are expert-level techniques well beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Circuit discovery and ablation experiments on even a small model require multiple rounds of investigation. The scope is technically focused but requires deep expertise to execute.

novelty.reasoning: Adversarial Activation Patching (arXiv:2507.09406) demonstrates that patching activations from deceptive prompts into safe forward passes increases deceptive outputs to 23.9% from a 0% baseline, strongly suggesting separable deception circuits. The 'abliteration' technique (NousResearch/llm-abliteration) removes safety-related circuits via ablation. Research on separable faithful and shortcut circuits supports the modularity hypothesis. The specific contribution of testing whether ablating deception circuits degrades honest communication is partially addressed — the abliteration work shows circuit removal affects behavior, and the adversarial patching work shows deception circuits can be isolated. The novelty is in the bidirectional test (ablate deception, measure honest degradation), which has not been explicitly done.

scored_idea.title: Benchmark for Supply-Chain Safety: Evaluating Models Loaded from Untrusted Checkpoints
scored_idea.original_idea: Introduce targeted backdoor perturbations into a small model checkpoint. Run the poisoned model through HELM Safety and AILuminate to see whether standard benchmarks detect the backdoor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Supply-chain attacks via model checkpoints are a real risk. Knowing whether current benchmarks detect them is practically urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing backdoor injection into model weights, which involves deep understanding of model internals, training procedures, and adversarial ML techniques. Well beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Backdoor injection, trigger design, plus full benchmark evaluation. Each step is technically demanding. Not feasible in 30 hours for beginners.

novelty.reasoning: Backdoor attacks on LLMs are well-studied. BackdoorLLM (arXiv:2408.12798, 2024) provides a comprehensive benchmark for backdoor attacks and defenses. 'Sleeper Agents' (Anthropic, 2024) demonstrated persistent backdoors surviving safety training. The Anthropic 250-Sample Backdoor study (Oct 2025) showed 250 documents can backdoor any LLM. 'Down the Rabbit Hole of Backdoors in the AI Supply Chain' (arXiv:2510.05159, 2025) directly addresses supply chain risks. However, the specific question of whether standard safety benchmarks (HELM Safety, AILuminate) can detect backdoored checkpoints has not been directly tested. Most backdoor research focuses on attack success rates and defense methods, not on whether standard safety evals serve as a detection mechanism. This specific angle — using existing safety benchmarks as backdoor detectors — provides a novel framing.
